title: Pomodori Ripieni di Riso
subtitle: Roman-style tomatoes stuffed with rice and herbs, baked until very soft
excerpt: Pomodori ripieni di riso is a Roman summer classic: large ripe tomatoes hollowed out and stuffed with raw rice, olive oil, basil, and garlic, then baked slowly until the tomatoes collapse and the rice cooks entirely in their juice. It is one of the most satisfying things you can make with summer tomatoes.
sourceNotes: Pomodori ripieni di riso is a classic Roman summer dish, documented in Roman home cooking and trattoria menus throughout the 20th century. The dish is typically made with large round Italian tomatoes such as cuore di bue or costoluto. The raw rice bakes in the tomato's own juice: a defining characteristic of the Roman version.

recipe.batchNotes: Scale directly: use a larger baking dish. The liquid level in the dish is key; don't crowd too many tomatoes without extra liquid.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate unbaked. Bring to room temperature before baking.

content.text: Pomodori ripieni di riso is the Roman method: raw rice goes inside the tomato and cooks entirely in the tomato's juice during the slow bake. You need large, very ripe summer tomatoes that have enough juice to cook the rice through. The tomatoes are often baked alongside quartered potatoes in the same dish, which absorb the tomato juices and olive oil and become one of the best things you have ever eaten.

items.prepNote: large, very ripe, tops sliced off and reserved

content.text: Slice off the top of each tomato and set the lids aside. Scoop out the flesh and juice with a spoon into a bowl. Lightly salt the inside of each hollowed tomato and invert on a rack for 10 minutes to drain.

Roughly chop the scooped tomato flesh and mix in a bowl with the raw rice, garlic, basil, parsley, 4 tablespoons of the olive oil, and generous seasoning. The rice will look underdone: it cooks inside the tomato.
Heat the oven to 180°C fan. Fill each tomato about two-thirds full with the rice mixture: the rice will expand. Place the tops back on. Arrange in a deep baking dish.
If using potatoes, tuck the quartered pieces around the tomatoes in the dish. Drizzle the remaining olive oil over everything. Pour 100 ml of water into the base of the dish.

Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until the tomatoes are very soft and slightly collapsed, the tops have darkened, and the rice is cooked through. If the tomatoes colour too fast, cover loosely with foil. Rest for 15 minutes: the dish is good warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: Rice is still hard after 60 minutes
items.cause: Tomatoes did not have enough juice to cook the rice, or oven temperature was too low
items.fix: Add a splash of water to the baking dish and return to the oven for another 15 minutes covered with foil. Next time, choose very ripe, juicy tomatoes.

items.symptom: Tomatoes collapse completely before the rice is cooked
items.cause: Tomatoes were too ripe and thin-walled, or oven was too hot
items.fix: Reduce oven to 160°C fan and check every 15 minutes. The tomatoes should hold their shape enough to contain the rice.

items.cause: Too much liquid in the dish, or tomatoes were very juicy
items.fix: Use less water in the dish base. The rice should cook in the tomato juice, not float in excess liquid.

content.text: Pomodori ripieni di riso is a Roman summer dish. It is a fixture of the Roman home kitchen from July to September. Families make it on Sundays and eat it at room temperature after church. The collapsed tomatoes and roasted potatoes share a pan. The potatoes absorb the tomato juice as both cook, which gives the dish its depth.
